JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed u/s 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a RTA.

2. The case of the petitioner in the nutshell is that on 26.07.2022 at about 12.30 p.m, as the petitioner was stood proceeding by the side of the outer ring road, by observing all the traffic rules and regulations in order to cross the road, opposite to Lorry Owner Association Office, Modern Bed Factory Bus Stop, Outer Ring Road, Bengaluru City.

entities.text: Lorry Owner Association Office, Modern Bed Factory Bus Stop
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: At that time the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-JZ-8921 came with high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner.
Due to tremendous impact petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately the rider of the motorcycle was shifted the injured to Kumar Clinic, wherein first aid was provided, then the rider of motorcycle assured the injured don't give complaint to the police he will spent medical expenditure.
As the assurance the petitioner went to his home, due to severe pain,

he went to Mathrushree Hospital and then to Girinagar Radhakrishna Hospital and thereafter to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital and then to Jayadeva Hospital and further to KC General Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.
In the said hospital he underwent several clinical examinations and was underwent surgery and thereafter discharged with and advice to regular follow up treatment.
He has spent substantial amount towards medical and other incidental expenses.

He further submitted that he was hale and healthy and was working as driver and earning Rs.30,000/-
per month.
Due to the accidental injuries he lost income from the date of accident.
He fully disabled to avocation and loss earning capacity.
Looking to the nature of injuries he permanently disabled.

The accident was caused due to rash and negligence riding of the rider of the motorcycle, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of the vehicle are jointly & severally liable to pay compensation.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence zhe was placed exparte.
4. The respondent No.2 appeared through his counsel and filed written statement admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-JZ-8921.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.

Further this respondent denied the negligence on the part of the rider of the insured vehicle and contended that the accident took place due to the negligence of petitioner himself who was crossing the road where there was no zebra crossing or provision for crossing the road.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the rider of motorcycle did not possess valid & effective DL.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.

The jurisdictional police after investigation they have filed charge sheet against the Thilakh who is the rider and owner of insured vehicle u/s 279, 338 of IPC and u/s 134(B), 187, 115, 177, 3(1), 181, 5 r/w Honnappa vs Padma on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176334606/
2 section 180 of IMV Act.
Non -compliance of sections 147, 149, 134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act is pleaded.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 26.07.2022 at about 12.30 p.m, Opposite Lorry Owners Association office, Modern Bed Factory Bus stop, Outer Ring Road, Bengaluru City due to actionable negligence of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-JZ-8921 ?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for ?
If so, at what rate and from whom ?
3) What order or award ?
6. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 19 were marked on his behalf.
Dr.Ramesh. B was examined as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P.20 & 21 documents.
In order to prove the defence, the respondent No.2 insurance company got examined the its Legal Manager as RW.1 and through him got marked Ex.R.1 document.
7. Heard counsel for the petitioner and respondent No.2 on merits.
The respondent No.2 filed written arguments.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.1 : The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint lodged by petitioner himself, the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against charge sheet against the Thilakh who is the rider and owner of insured vehicle u/s 279, 338 of IPC and u/s 134(B), 187, 115, 177, 3(1), 181, 5 r/w section 180 of IMV Act.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Though the respondent No.2 has denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove its defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioner.
Therefore, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the rider of the motorcycle.

In addenda, in a claim for compensation u/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required Honnappa vs Padma on 3 October, 2025

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176334606/
3
as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2011) 3 SCC 646.

With this observation issue No.1 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
9. ISSUE NO.2 :
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the rider of the motorcycle.
Therefore he is entitled for compensation.
10. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME :

The petitioner has produced his Aadhaar card and Driving Licence which are marked as Ex.P.18 and 19, as per the above said documents, the date of the petitioner is mentioned as 28.01.1978 and 01.08.1975.
The said two documents of the petitioner disclose the different date of birth.

Therefore, those documents cannot be considered for the purpose of the age of the petitioner, thereby I proceed to rely on the medical documents and police documents and those documents are disclosed as age of the petitioner is 48.
Further the petitioner has mentioned his age in column No.3 of the petition as 48 years.
Hence, I rely on the police and medical documents of the petitioner for the purpose of the age.
So, age of the petitioner is 48 years at the time of accident.

Hence, the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is "13".
11.
The petitioner deposed that prior to the accident she was working as Lorry driver and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
No documents have been produced to establish the avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in his evidence affidavit.
It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA. No.101144/2020 (MV) dated. 05.07.2023.

Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred in the year 2022.
Therefore, Rs.15,500/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the petitioner.

12. As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the following injuries : Multiple abrasions over the face, abrasions over the right elbow joint and upper 1/3rd of right forearm,
contusion of left forearm, multiple abrasion over the right leg.
It is needless to say that the injury No.1, 2 and 4 are simple and injury No.3 is grievous in nature.

He has produced Ex.P13 Discharge summary, discloses that he has taken treatment as an inpatient in K.C.General Hospital for the Honnappa vs Padma on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176334606/
4 period from 04.08.2022 to 09.08.2022 (6 days in total).

entities.text: K.C.General Hospital for the Honnappa vs Padma
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As per discharge summary during the course of treatment he had undergone surgeries in the form of : ORIF with DCF Left.
13. It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has thereby lost his earning capacity.

Therefore he got examined Dr.Ramesh. B as PW.2 who stated that on clinical examination conducted by him, he found that petitioner has sustained total permanent physical disability of 20% of left upper limb and 7% disability to the whole body.
During the course of cross examination PW.2 categorically admitted that he has not treated the petitioner and also he has not issued disability certificate to the petitioner.
Further he has also not seen the inpatient records.
He he admitted that as per X-ray fracture is united, with implants in situ and the petitioner can do his day-to-day activities with certain difficulties.
However from the careful examination of the medical records, it is seen that PW.2 has assessed the disability on the higher side.

Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 5%, cannot be ruled out.

Therefore, I consider the functional disability of the petitioner at 5%.
14.
ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
The period of hospitalization of 6 days is proved.

During his stay in the hospital the petitioner would have incurred expenses towards attendant charges as some family member of the petitioner would have accompanied him to the hospital to take his care by leaving their duties.

During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet,
transportation and nutrition.
Considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.1,000/- per day and a sum of Rs.6,000/- (1,000 X 6) under this head.
15. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony.

Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.50,000/- under this head.
16. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 2 months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner,
this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.31,000/- (15,500 X 2) under this head.
17. MEDICAL EXPENSES :

As per the bills marked at Ex.P11, the petitioner has spent Rs.9,497/-
towards medical expenses.
All these bills have been examined with care and are found to be correct.
Hence the petitioner is entitled Rs.9,497/- which is rounded off to Rs.9,500/- towards medical expenses.

sentences.text: LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '13'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.15,500/- p.m.
Hence a sum of Rs.1,20,900/- (Rs.15,500 X 12 X 13 X 5/100) is awarded under this head.

19. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Hence a sum of Rs.40,000/- is awarded under this head.
20. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES :
The doctor witness stated that the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants.
No estimation is produced to show the future medical expenses.
But undisputedly petitioner has to undergo surgery for removal of implants, for which he has to necessarily bear certain expenses.
During the course of cross examination PW.2 stated that if implants will remove in their hospital, expenses will normal i.e., around Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/-.
Thus he is entitled to Rs.10,000/- towards future medical and other incidental expenses.

21. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Attendant charges, extra nutritious : 6,000-00 food & conveyance charges 2 Pain &
sufferings : 50,000-00 3 Loss of income during laid-up : 31,000-00 period 4
Medical expenses : 9,500-00 5 Loss of future income due to : 1,20,900-00 disability 6 Loss of future amenities & : 40,000-00 happiness 7
Future medical and other : 10,000-00 incidental expenses Total 2,67,400-00 22.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
23. While answering the issue No.2 this Tribunal comes to the conclusion that accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider of motorcycle.

The respondent No.2 admitted the issuance of policy in respect of the offending vehicle and contended that as on the date of accident the rider of the motorcycle was not holding driving license, hence it is violation of terms and conditions of the policy as such they are not liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
In support of this contention the respondent No.2 got examined its official as RW.1.
During his cross examination he admitted that police have filed charge sheet against their insured vehicle but the rider was not possessing valid DL.
Further he denied that the petitioner was the third party and they are liable to pay compensation.

It is pertinent to note herein in the charge sheet it is clearly mentioned the rider was not possessing valid driving licence as on the date of accident, but in this regard they have not enquired the concerned RTO office about DL of offending vehicle driver.

In this regard he has relied on the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Spl. Leave petition (Civil) No.11757/2025 in the case Honnappa vs Padma on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176334606/
6 of Mahaveer V/s Branch Manager, United India Ins.Co.Ltd, wherein the Honble Apex Court observed that even though owner of the vehicle having being the party before the Tribunal, no evidence was given regarding driving licence of the driver.

sentences.text: The owner did not mount the box nor was any licence produced either of the person who was driving the vehicle or the person to whom it was entrusted.
The owner thus failed to prove that the vehicle was entrusted to a person having valid licence.
Hence Hon'ble Apex Court dismissed the appeal filed by the owner of the vehicle and made liable the owner to pay the compensation.

24. On the other hand the petitioner relied on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA.No.202104/2024 (MV) in the case of The Branch Manager ICICI Lombard Gen.Ins.CO.Ltd.,
v/s Pooja and others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka observed that as M.V.Act is a benevolent legislation the claimants cannot deprived of the compensation so awarded in this case.

entities.text:
Branch Manager ICICI Lombard Gen.Ins.CO.Ltd.,
v/s Pooja and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore the Hon'ble High Court liable the insurance company and to pay the compensation and directed to recover from the owner.

In the said case is also accident occurred after the amendment of the M.V.Act.
25.
In the present case also as per the charge sheet the rider of the motorcycle was not having valid DL as on the date of accident.
The owner of the vehicle was party but he was placed exparte.
The judgment relied by the petitioner is of our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka passed on 19.09.2024.
The decision relied by the respondent No.2 is of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India dated 24.04.2025.
Hence it is the recent judgment and decision of Hon'ble Apex Court.
Therefore this Court has to relied on the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court.

26. It is relevant to relied on the Citation No.FAO-1081- 2024 (O & M) in the case of Universal Sompo Gen.Ins.Co.Ltd. V/s Anuj Rani and other with respect to amendment of sec.150 and stated that the tribunal directed the appellant / Insurance company to pay the award amount to claimants and then to recover from driver / owner.

entities.text: Universal Sompo Gen.Ins.Co.Ltd. V/s Anuj Rani and other
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Further it is to be noted that in the said case that the accident took place on 27.05.2022 and the amendment to Motor Vehicles Act came into force w.e.f 01.04.2022.
27.
Reverting back to the factual matrix, this Court also does not loose sight of the fact that the accident had happened on 26.07.2022.
The amendment to the MV Act, came into force on 01.04.2022.
The amendment to Sec.150 of MV Act makes it crystal clear that, if a person drives a vehicle without DL, than there is no question of making insurance company liable.
Further the provision makes it clear that there is no question of even pay and recovery also.
This accident is subsequent to that of the amendment to the IMV Act.
When such being the case, the Respondent No.2 cannot be made liable.

28. Further respondent No.2 has relied on the judgment of M.F.A.No.3297/2019 in the case of Smt.Adilakshmamma and Others Vs., Sri. Raju and other and contended that when the owner knowing that rider of the motorcycle was not holding driving license and handed over his motorcycle to the rider who was not having driving license then the owner is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

entities.text: Smt.Adilakshmamma and Others Vs., Sri. Raju and other
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In this case on hand also the respondent No.1 is the owner of the motorcycle and he is knowing well that the rider was not having driving license and permitted the Honnappa vs Padma on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176334606/
7 rider to ride her motorcycle and the rider caused this accident, hence the respondent No.2 is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioner, but the respondent No.1 who is the owner of the motorcycle is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The said authority relied by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 is applicable to the present case on hand.
As such the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation.

Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
29. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,67,400/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.1 i.e., the RC owner of the Motorcycle is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
After deposit, the entire compensation amount together with interest shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.decision:
The judgment relied by the petitioner is of our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka passed on 19.09.2024.
As such the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation.
Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
29. ISSUE NO.3 :
In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,67,400/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.1 i.e., the RC owner of the Motorcycle is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
After deposit, the entire compensation amount together with interest shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
